cands.bio: Democratic U.S. representative from California, in Congress since 1995 and now representing District 18. Immigration lawyer, former law faculty member and congressional staffer, and Santa Clara County supervisor from 1981 to 1994. Long-time House Judiciary member; Ranking Member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee.

controversies.text: Missed 10 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.5%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 2, 2025-05-15 to 2025-05-15.

In December 2021, news reports said Lofgren, a leading Democratic opponent of big-tech antitrust bills, has a daughter who is corporate counsel at Google. Lofgren said every decision she makes is for her district, not anyone else. She said her daughter works on contracts and is not involved in Google's antitrust fights.

A 2007 watchdog report found her campaign paid her husband's two firms about $350,000 over six years for compliance, event and office services. Federal rules allow paying relatives at fair market value for real work. Lofgren said the work was legal and proper, and that her husband closed his firm in 2006.

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO (2026)

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Lofgren on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth limits or land conservation, gun laws, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2026, 2024, 2022 or 2020. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through, so some of her earlier-session records could not be read. Her 2013 abortion-ban floor role and her stated reaction to Roe v. Wade come from Wikipedia, which gives no underlying source for them in the text we read.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 18th Congressional District in 2026. U.S. Marine Corps veteran (1990–1995) and electrical and failure-analysis engineer in medical-device and tech R&D. Former small-business music teacher and church elder in San Jose. Ran for Santa Clara County Board of Education in 2024. Has held no public office.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California endorsed Lewis in the 2026 race, per Ballotpedia's endorsement list. Ballotpedia also lists several voter-guide recommendations, including April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Liberty For All and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Shane Lewis was raised or when he moved to California. We found no record of him holding any public office. His 2024 run for county school board was unsuccessful. His campaign themes cover immigration reform, a flat tax on wages, and water and energy, but the pages we had are general. They do not cover H-1B visas or immigration enforcement specifics, property taxes, data centers, development limits, guns, abortion, school vouchers or charters, or police funding. We found no reporting of controversies and no foreign ties. We did not have his campaign website, so his platform is known only from his Ballotpedia survey answers.
